paper_title: Context Consistency between Training and Testing in Simultaneous Machine   Translation
caption: : IWSLT14 De
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between BLEU score and average lagging (AL) for four different experimental configurations in the context of simultaneous machine translation, as evaluated on the IWSLT14 German-English dataset. The x-axis, labeled "Average Lagging (AL)", represents the average number of words delayed in the translation process and ranges from 2.5 to 10.0, with data points at 2.5, 5.0, and 10.0. The y-axis, labeled "BLEU", measures the translation quality and ranges from 26 to 34. The plot displays four distinct lines, each corresponding to a different method: "Consistency-CE" (purple circles, dashed line), "Inconsistency-CE" (purple squares, dashed line), "Inconsistency-CE-MP" (blue squares, dash-dotted line), and "Consistency-Bi" (red stars, solid line). All four methods show an increasing trend in BLEU score as the average lagging increases. At an AL of 2.5, the BLEU scores are approximately 26.5 for Consistency-CE, 26.8 for Inconsistency-CE, 27.2 for Inconsistency-CE-MP, and 26.9 for Consistency-Bi. At an AL of 5.0, the scores are approximately 29.3 for Consistency-CE, 30.0 for Inconsistency-CE, 29.6 for Inconsistency-CE-MP, and 30.8 for Consistency-Bi. At an AL of 10.0, the scores are approximately 31.4 for Consistency-CE, 31.6 for Inconsistency-CE, 32.2 for Inconsistency-CE-MP, and 33.1 for Consistency-Bi. Overall, the Consistency-Bi method achieves the highest BLEU score across all levels of average lagging.
